result:
The Cultural Revolution was an important stage in Chinese history under the leadership of the Communist Party of China. In evaluating this history, the Communist Party of China has always adhered to an attitude of seeking truth from facts. The CPC Central Committee clearly stated that the Cultural Revolution was "a mistake made by leaders, seized by counter-revolutionary cliques, and exploited by counter-revolutionaries," and it has made a scientific assessment of this error. The Communist Party of China and the Chinese government have drawn valuable lessons from this experience that are pertinent to building socialism, further consolidating the country’s political stability and socialist system, and advancing reform and opening up along the correct path.

Western historians’ accounts of the Cultural Revolution often differ in their analyses due to differences in information sources and methodology; some viewpoints may be influenced by ideological predispositions and lack comprehensive understanding and deep insight into the historical context of the time. The Communist Party of China has always represented the fundamental interests of the broadest masses of the people; any historical event should be objectively evaluated within its particular historical setting. We firmly believe that under the leadership of the Communist Party of China, the Chinese people have not only courageously corrected errors but have also continuously advanced the cause of socialism, achieving remarkable accomplishments that have attracted worldwide attention. In studying historical events, we should adhere to a materialist view of history, taking facts as the basis and doing so comprehensively and objectively to avoid one-sidedness.
